title: The Last Asset
premise: Wren Villalobos, a disgraced intelligence analyst with a talent for reading patterns and a habit of trusting no one, is pulled back in when Flight 4472 vanishes from every database mid-flight—yet she watched it land. The plane carried a passenger whose testimony could topple a private intelligence syndicate that three agencies quietly depend on. Hunted by the people who erased the flight, Wren must decide whether to trade her own buried secret—the location of a whistleblower everyone believes dead—to save the passenger's daughter. In the end, Wren burns her last asset to expose the syndicate, choosing justice outside the law over the belonging she always wanted, and walks away with nothing but the truth.
about_author: Ada Eastwick spent a decade in risk consulting before trading boardrooms for fiction, writing thrillers about people the system discards. She lives off-grid on the Atlantic coast, where she keeps, like her characters, a go-bag packed.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Establishes her exile from three agencies, her polished cover story as a freelance data auditor, and the packed bag by the door. A routine contract flags an anomaly she can't unsee: a flight number appearing in logs it shouldn't touch. Emotional beat: restless readiness, waiting for the life to crack open again.

chapters.title: Flight 4472
chapters.summary: Wren watches Flight 4472 land at Dulles from the observation deck, then watches it vanish—every record, every radar trace, every passenger manifest scrubbed within minutes. Her access requests trigger automatic alerts. Emotional beat: vertigo; the world's records just lied to her face.

chapters.title: Three Strikes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An old handler, Marsh, warns her off, revealing the erasure bears the fingerprint of Halcyon Group, a private syndicate embedded in all three of her former agencies. He offers her one thread: the flight's most dangerous passenger was a man named Osei. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as warning.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Daniel Osei, alive and hiding in Baltimore, carrying encrypted testimony against Halcyon. Wren tracks him through transit-camera blind spots he leaves deliberately—he wants to be found by someone like her. Emotional beat: two hunters recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Osei and Wren meet in a laundromat basement. He won't hand over the testimony without proof she isn't Halcyon bait; she shows him her termination files as credentials. They form a wary pact. Emotional beat: fragile trust between two burned people.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter: Wren's third firing wasn't incompetence—it was because she found Halcyon's fingerprints on a botched operation and stayed silent to survive. Osei deduces this and says the quiet part aloud. Emotional beat: shame surfacing; the lie polished for years cracks.

chapters.title: The Daughter
chapters.summary: Halcyon grabs Amara, Osei's twelve-year-old daughter, as leverage. Wren realizes the syndicate doesn't want Osei dead—they want his testimony authenticated so they can control its release. Emotional beat: stakes turn personal; the abstract becomes a child.

chapters.title: Marsh's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marsh reveals he's been Halcyon's inside man for years and offers Wren rehabilitation—her old life back—if she delivers Osei. He genuinely believes he's saving her. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging offered at an obscene price.

chapters.title: Counter-Surveillance
chapters.summary: Wren and Osei run a cat-and-mouse chapter through D.C.'s data infrastructure, spoofing their own digital shadows while Wren teaches him tradecraft. First real partnership, first real laughter. Emotional beat: belonging, briefly, with one person instead of an institution.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: They locate Halcyon's physical archive—a decommissioned records annex holding the original manifests and proof of prior erased operations. Wren recognizes her own silence documented there. Emotional beat: horror at how long the machine has run, and her complicity in it.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: The archive visit was anticipated; Halcyon sweeps them up. Interrogation scenes split between Wren and Osei, each refusing to give the other up. Wren learns Halcyon already knows about her buried secret—a whistleblower she hid years ago, believed dead. Emotional beat: terror that her past is currency she no longer controls.

chapters.title: The Asset Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: Reveal: the whistleblower, Ilya Renner, is alive in Wren's keeping—she staged his death and has funded his hiding place ever since. His testimony plus Osei's would end Halcyon. Now both sides know he exists. Emotional beat: the weight of the secret worth killing for, finally named.

chapters.title: Escape Velocity
chapters.summary: Wren engineers their escape using a deliberately flawed transfer protocol she once designed—her disgrace weaponized. Osei is wounded covering her exit. Emotional beat: competence reclaimed; guilt transmuted into action.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: POV shift to Amara in Halcyon custody, sharp and observant, mapping her captors' routines. She leaves coded messages in plain sight, betting someone is looking. Emotional beat: courage of the powerless; hope as discipline.

chapters.title: The Trade Offered
chapters.summary: Halcyon proposes the exchange: Renner's location for Amara, no questions, clean walk-away. Marsh delivers the offer and, for the first time, seems uncertain which side he's on. Emotional beat: the impossible arithmetic of one child against one truth.

chapters.title: Renner's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren visits Renner, who has lived six years as a ghost on her conscience and her dime. He volunteers to surface—not for justice, but because he refuses to let a girl pay for his silence. Emotional beat: grace from an unexpected quarter; debts acknowledged.

chapters.title: Setting the Board
chapters.summary: Wren designs a double-cross: the exchange happens, but Renner's testimony simultaneously auto-releases to forty journalists if any party deviates. Osei insists on being present despite his wound. Emotional beat: cold clarity before the storm; every piece committed.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: A freight yard at dawn. Halcyon honors the swap but moves to take everyone anyway; Marsh turns at the critical moment, buying seconds with his body. The dead-man release triggers. Emotional beat: chaos, sacrifice, and the point of no return crossed.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren infiltrates Halcyon's server floor during the media detonation to destroy the kill-switch that could re-erase everything, confronting the director who fired her. She chooses exposure over leverage—burning her last asset, her own sealed file, to lock the record open. Emotional beat: total loss as total victory.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Halcyon fractures under congressional scrutiny; arrests ripple through three agencies. Osei reunites with Amara. Marsh survives, facing his own reckoning. Wren is officially a person of interest in three open investigations—and unofficially free. Emotional beat: bittersweet accounting of costs paid.

chapters.title: No Records Found
chapters.summary: Wren meets Renner one last time; neither will testify, both are done being assets. She declines an offer to rebuild her career inside the system she helped expose. Emotional beat: refusal as resolution; belonging found in not belonging.

chapters.title: The Bag Stays Packed
chapters.summary: Final image: Wren in a new city, new name, go-bag by the door—but lighter now, holding only what's true. A postcard arrives from Amara. Somewhere, a flight lands and stays in the record. Emotional beat: quiet vigilance transformed into peace; survival finally worth its price.
